name: Outline
description: A knowledge base for teams: nested documents in collections, a clean Markdown-friendly editor with real-time collaboration, strong search and public sharing. It is a document wiki, not a database tool.
licenseNote: Business Source License 1.1. You may self-host it for your own organisation, but not offer it to third parties as a hosted document service. Each release converts to Apache-2.0 on its change date, roughly four years later. This is not an OSI-approved open-source licence.
backing: General Outline, Inc., a small company funded by its hosted service

maturity.rationale: Polished, released steadily for years and used by many companies. A small team maintains it, and self-hosters depend on that team's licensing decisions.

selfHosting.summary: It needs PostgreSQL, Redis, file storage and, the part that surprises people, a sign-in provider: OIDC, Google, Microsoft, Slack or similar. Outline does not manage passwords itself. If you do not already run an identity provider, that becomes a second project.

managedHosting.label: Outline Cloud
managedHosting.note: Run by the developers; paid per user

strengths: A fast, uncluttered editor with Markdown shortcuts and real-time collaboration
Imports Notion and Confluence exports and keeps the page hierarchy
Collections, granular permissions, public share links and a solid API
weaknesses: Source-available, not open source: see the licence note
No databases, boards or other Notion-style structured views
Self-hosting requires an external sign-in provider
No offline mode and no native mobile apps

featureNotes.plain-files: Stored in a database; exports to Markdown
